placements.note: A dwelling built for habitation. From Old English hus, from Proto-Germanic *hustiz, from PIE *bhudh- (to hide, shelter).
Provided with shelter; put into a house. From house + -ed.
Dwellings collectively; or a protective covering. From house + -ing.
Without a house; homeless. From house + -less.
A domestic group; a family and those who live in a house. From house + hold.
The head of a household. From household + -er.
One who manages a household; a domestic servant. From house + keeper.
Work done in managing a household. From house + work.
A party celebrating moving into a new house. From house + warming.
A married woman who manages a household. From house + wife.
Existing or done within an organization. From in- + house.
A large building for storing goods. From ware + house (warehouse = goods-house).
Stored in a warehouse. From warehouse + -ed.
Storing in a warehouse. From warehouse + -ing.
A building used for storage. From store + house.
A small structure outside a main building; a latrine. From out- + house.
